**Equifax acquires AccountScore to embed open banking data in credit decisions**

*The acquisition gives one of the world's three major credit bureaux direct ownership of open banking analytics capability, signalling that transaction data is becoming core infrastructure for credit assessment rather than a supplementary input.*

Equifax has acquired AccountScore, a UK-based open banking data analytics firm. The deal brings AccountScore's transaction categorisation and income verification tools inside a global credit bureau operation, integrating permissioned bank data directly into Equifax's decisioning products.

AccountScore has built its business on turning raw open banking feeds into structured affordability and creditworthiness signals – the kind of enrichment layer that lenders increasingly expect alongside traditional credit files. For Equifax, the acquisition removes a dependency on third-party open banking intermediaries and positions it to offer combined bureau-plus-bank-data products as a single service.

The deal fits a broader pattern of credit data incumbents acquiring open banking capability rather than building it. PayPoint completed its acquisition of AperiData in June for similar reasons. As open finance regulation widens the data pools available – pensions, investments, insurance – the commercial logic of owning the analytics layer, not just accessing the pipes, becomes harder for the major bureaux to ignore.

*Sources: [Equifax acquires Open Banking and Data analytics company…](https://ffnews.com/newsarticle/equifax-acquires-open-banking-and-data-analytics-company-accountscore) — Fintech Finance News*

**Tieto and Siirto partner to connect e-invoicing with instant payments in Finland**

*Embedding instant payment functionality into structured billing flows could accelerate commercial account-to-account adoption beyond person-to-person transfers in one of Europe's most digitised invoicing markets.*

Tieto, the Nordic technology firm, is partnering with Siirto, Finland's instant payment method with more than one million registered users, to integrate instant payment functionality into digital invoicing workflows. The partnership aims to let businesses and consumers settle e-invoices directly through Siirto's real-time rails.

Instant payments adoption in most European markets has been driven by person-to-person transfers, but embedding them into structured billing flows – where the payment amount, recipient and reference are pre-populated from the invoice – removes friction that has slowed business-to-consumer and business-to-business uptake. Finland's relatively high e-invoicing penetration makes it a natural market to test this integration.

Siirto operates on Finland's domestic instant payment infrastructure, which connects to the broader SEPA instant credit transfer scheme. The partnership is an example of how instant payments volumes may grow not through new consumer propositions but through tighter integration with existing commercial workflows such as invoicing, subscriptions and recurring billing.

*Sources: [Tieto and Siirto Partner to Revolutionize E-Invoicing and Instant Payments in Finland](https://ffnews.com/news/tieto-and-siirto-partner-to-improve-e-invoicing-experience-in-finland-cdda197e) — Ffnews | [Tieto and Siirto partner to improve e-invoicing experience in Finland](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110731/tieto-and-siirto-partner-to-improve-e-invoicing-experience-in-finland?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**Trustly publishes second-quarter results as pay-by-bank volumes continue to grow**

*The second-quarter report offers a read on the health of Europe's largest independent pay-by-bank platform.*

Trustly has published its second-quarter 2026 results for the period ending June 30. The Swedish firm, which operates one of Europe's largest open banking payment platforms, processes pay-by-bank transactions across multiple markets for merchants in e-commerce, financial services and gaming.

The release comes during a period of heightened activity in the pay-by-bank segment. Competitors including TrueLayer, Plaid and GoCardless have each announced product expansions or commercial milestones in recent months, while the launch of the UK Payments Initiative has created a new domestic scheme-level competitor to card networks. Trustly's quarterly disclosure provides a benchmark for how the independent pay-by-bank model is performing against this backdrop.

Full financial details were not available in the feed summary. Trustly remains privately held following its 2018 acquisition by Nordic Capital, and its periodic reporting offers one of the few regular windows into the economics of a scaled European pay-by-bank operation.

*Sources: [STOCKHOLM, 27 August 2026 - Trustly Holding AB Publ. They should only be covered if the results are notable – a record profit, surprising turnaround, unexpected loss, etc. And, even then, only if the company is itself a large or particularly interesting player in the sector.

**Bundesbank urges banks to take more active role in European payments development**

*The intervention adds institutional weight to the payment sovereignty debate as Wero expands and the digital euro advances through the European Parliament.*

The Deutsche Bundesbank has called on banks and payment service providers to engage more actively in developing Europe's payments infrastructure. The intervention, reported by The Banker, comes amid intensifying debate over European payment autonomy and the role of domestic schemes versus global card networks.

Germany is a critical market for several overlapping European payments initiatives. Wero, the European Payments Initiative's digital wallet, went live for German customers through ING in August 2025 and is expanding to further banks. The digital euro advanced to trilogue negotiations in July after the European Parliament's vote. In both cases, bank participation and investment are prerequisites for success – and the Bundesbank's public nudge suggests the pace of engagement from the German banking sector has not matched the ambition of the policy framework.

The statement echoes similar calls from the Bank of Finland and the French Banking Federation, both of which framed European payment sovereignty as a strategic priority. The Bundesbank's voice carries particular weight given the size of the German payments market and the historically cautious posture of its banking sector toward pan-European payment projects.

*Sources: [Reg Wrap: US kills targeted credit programme guidance](https://www.thebanker.com/content/0278b427-84f3-44a3-87e7-5115b1e81b21) — The Banker*
